claim: Administration of three doses of RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine given at one-month intervals (standard regimen) provided 62.5% protection in the Malaria-071 trial.
source: Malaria-071, a controlled human malaria infection trial, demonstrated that administration of three doses of RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine given at one-month intervals was inferior to a delayed fractional dose (DFD) schedule (62.5% vs 86.7% protection, respectively).
evidence: The manuscript directly states the protection rate observed in the standard regimen of the Malaria-071 trial.

claim: The delayed fractional dose (DFD) schedule of RTS,S/AS01 vaccine provided 86.7% protection in the Malaria-071 trial.
source: Malaria-071, a controlled human malaria infection trial, demonstrated that administration of three doses of RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine given at one-month intervals was inferior to a delayed fractional dose (DFD) schedule (62.5% vs 86.7% protection, respectively).
evidence: The manuscript directly states the protection rate observed in the DFD regimen of the Malaria-071 trial.

claim: Protection in both vaccine regimens was associated with early induction of functional IL-21-secreting circumsporozoite (CSP)-specific pTfh cells.

evidence: The manuscript presents data showing correlation between IL-21-secreting CSP-specific pTfh cells and protection status.

claim: Protection in both vaccine regimens was associated with induction of CSP-specific memory B cell responses after the second dose that persisted after the third dose.
source: Here, we show that protection in both study arms was associated with early induction of functional IL-21-secreting circumsporozoite (CSP)-specific pTfh cells, together with induction of CSP-specific memory B cell responses after the second dose that persisted after the third dose.
